meta.title: Directive 2012/13/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 May 2012 on the right to information in criminal proceedings

items.text: This Directive lays down rules concerning the right to information of suspects or accused persons, relating to their rights in criminal proceedings and to the accusation against them. It also lays down rules concerning the right to information of persons subject to a European Arrest Warrant relating to their rights.
items.heading: Article 1

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 5/2015, de 27 de abril, por la que se modifican la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal y la Ley Orgánica 6/1985, de 1 de julio, del Poder Judicial, para transponer la Directiva 2010/64/UE, de 20 de octubre de 2010, relativa al derecho a interpretación y a traducción en los procesos penales y la Directiva 2012/13/UE, de 22 de mayo de 2012, relativa al derecho a la información en los procesos penales
nationalActs.titleEn: Organic Law 5/2015, of April 27, amending the Criminal Procedural Law and Organic Law 6/1985, of July 1, of the Judiciary, to transpose Directive 2010/64 / EU, of 20 of October 2010, regarding the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and Directive 2012/13 / EU, of May 22, 2012, concerning the right to information in criminal proceedings

nationalActs.title: Ley Orgánica 13/2015, de 5 de octubre, de modificación de la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal para el fortalecimiento de las garantías procesales y la regulación de las medidas de investigación tecnológica
nationalActs.titleEn: Organic Law 13/2015, of October 5, amending the Criminal Procedure Law for the strengthening of procedural safeguards and the regulation of technological investigation measures

nationalActs.title: Ley 3/2018, de 11 de junio, por la que se modifica la Ley 23/2014, de 20 de noviembre, de reconocimiento mutuo de resoluciones penales en la Unión Europea, para regular la Orden Europea de Investigación
nationalActs.titleEn: Law 3/2018, of June 11, amending Law 23/2014, of November 20, on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union, to regulate the European Investigation Order

items.comment: This directive has been transposed in a phased manner through two laws that modified the Criminal Procedural Law (specifically, articles 118, 302, 505, 520, 520 ter, 527 and 775) and a third law that modified the Article 50 of the Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies from the time persons are made aware by the competent authorities of a Member State that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence until the conclusion of the proceedings, which is understood to mean the final determination of the question whether the suspect or accused person has committed the criminal offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: It is not expressly provided that the information should be provided until the conclusion of the proceedings
provisions.textEn: Any person to whom a punishable act is attributed may exercise the right of defense, intervening in the proceedings, since its existence is notified, has been subject to detention or any other precautionary measure or has been indicted. To this end, s/he must be informed, without undue delay, of the following rights: a) Right to be informed of the facts attributed to it, as well as of any relevant changes in the object of the investigation and of the alleged facts.

provisions.comment: Again, the moment from which the suspect must be informed is established, but not the extension of the right throughout the process.
provisions.textEn: The admission of complaint or suit, or any other procedural action from which the imputation of a crime against specific person or persons derives, will be immediately brought to the attention of those allegedly responsible

provisions.comment: The temporal extension with which the right of defense is recognized, and the fact that the right to be informed of the accusation is a necessary condition for the effective exercise of the right of defense, could serve to transpose this provision of the Directive.
provisions.textEn: The right of defense shall be exercised without more limitations than those expressly provided in the law from the attribution of the punishable act investigated to the extinction of the penalty.

items.text: 2. Where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction regarding minor offences by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed to such a court, this Directive shall apply only to the proceedings before that court, following such an appeal.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: In Spain, penal sanctions for minor offences are always imposed by Courts having jurisdiction in criminal matters, therefore this provision is not applicable

items.heading: Article 3

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons are provided promptly with information concerning at least the following procedural rights, as they apply under national law, in order to allow for those rights to be exercised effectively:

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Any person charged with a punishable act may exercise the right of defence, intervening in the proceedings, since its existence is notified, has been subject to detention or any other precautionary measure or has been indicted. To this end, s/he must be informed, without undue delay, of the following rights:

items.text:
(a)

the right of access to a lawyer;

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: d) Right to freely appoint a lawyer

items.text:
(b)

any entitlement to free legal advice and the conditions for obtaining such advice;

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: e) Right to request free legal assistance, procedure to do so and conditions to obtain it

items.text:
(c)

the right to be informed of the accusation, in accordance with Article 6;

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: a) Right to be informed of the facts attributed to him/her, as well as of any relevant changes in the object of the investigation and of the alleged facts. This information will be provided with sufficient detail to allow the effective exercise of the right of defence.

items.text:
(d)

the right to interpretation and translation;

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: f) Right to free translation and interpretation in accordance with the provisions of articles 123 and 127.

items.text:
(e)

the right to remain silent.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: g) Right to remain silent and not to give statements if s/he does not wish to do so, and not to answer any or some of the questions asked.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that the information provided for under paragraph 1 shall be given orally or in writing, in simple and accessible language, taking into account any particular needs of vulnerable suspects or vulnerable accused persons.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: The information referred to in this section will be provided in an understandable and accessible language. To this end, the information will be adapted to the age of the recipient, his/her degree of maturity, disability and any other personal circumstance from which a modification of the ability to understand the relevance of the information provided may result.

items.heading: Article 4

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons who are arrested or detained are provided promptly with a written Letter of Rights. They shall be given an opportunity to read the Letter of Rights and shall be allowed to keep it in their possession throughout the time that they are deprived of liberty.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Any person detained or imprisoned shall be informed in writing, in a simple and accessible language, in a language that s/he understands and immediately, of the facts attributed to him/her and the reasons for his/her deprivation of liberty, , as well as his/her rights and specially the following: (...)
In any case, the detainee will be allowed to keep in his/her possession the written declaration of rights during the entire time of the detention.

items.text: 2. In addition to the information set out in Article 3, the Letter of Rights referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall contain information about the following rights as they apply under national law:

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Any person detained or imprisoned shall be informed in writing, in a simple and accessible language, in a language that s/he understands and immediately, of the facts attributed to him/her and the reasons for his/her deprivation of liberty, as well as his/her rights and specially the following: (...)

items.text:
(a)

the right of access to the materials of the case;

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: The right to access is limited to those materials of the case which are essential in order to challenge de detention
provisions.textEn: Any person detained or imprisoned shall be informed in writing, in a simple and accessible language, in a language that s/he understands and immediately, of the facts attributed to him/her and the reasons for his/her deprivation of liberty, as well as his/her rights and specially the following: (...) d) Right to access the elements of case that are essential to challenge the legality of the detention or deprivation of liberty

items.text:
(b)

the right to have consular authorities and one person informed;

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: e) The right to inform the family member or person which the defendant decides, without undue delay, of his/her deprivation of liberty and the place of custody in which s/he stays. Foreigners will have the right to inform of the above circumstances to the consular office of their country.

f) Right to communicate by telephone, without undue delay, with a third party of his/her choice. This communication shall be held in the presence of a police officer or, where appropriate, of the official designated by the judge or prosecutor
g) Right to be visited by the consular authorities of his/her country, to communicate and to mail with them.

items.text:
(c)

the right of access to urgent medical assistance; and

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: There are no reference to the urgency of the situation, so it may be considered that the right is wider according to the Spanish legislation
provisions.textEn: i) Right to be examined by a forensic doctor or his/her legal substitute and, failing that possibility, by the doctor of the institution in which the detained person is located, or by any other doctor dependent on the State or on other Public Administration.

items.text:
(d)

the maximum number of hours or days suspects or accused persons may be deprived of liberty before being brought before a judicial authority.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: Preventive detention, as a general rule, may not last more than the time strictly necessary to carry out the police investigation and, in no case, more than 72 hours (Article 520.1 II Criminal Procedural Law)
provisions.textEn: The detained person shall be informed of the maximum legal term of the detention until being brought before a judicial authority and of the procedure by which s/he may challenge the lawfulness of his/her detention.

items.text: 3. The Letter of Rights shall also contain basic information about any possibility, under national law, of challenging the lawfulness of the arrest; obtaining a review of the detention; or making a request for provisional release.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: d) Right of access to the elements that are essential to challenge the lawfullness of detention or deprivation of liberty.

The detained person shall be informed of the maximum legal term of the detention until being brought before a judicial authority and of the procedure by which s/he may challenge the lawfulness of his/her detention.

items.text: 4. The Letter of Rights shall be drafted in simple and accessible language. An indicative model Letter of Rights is set out in Annex I.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: Spanish law, although it requires the detainee to be informed of all the rights that correspond to him/her in writing, does not contain an annex with an indicative model Letter of Rights and does not use the term "Letter of Rights"
provisions.textEn: Any person detained or imprisoned shall be informed in writing, in a simple and accessible language, in a language that s/he understands and immediately, of the facts attributed to him/her and the reasons for his/her deprivation of liberty, as well as his/her rights and specially the following: (...)

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons receive the Letter of Rights written in a language that they understand. Where a Letter of Rights is not available in the appropriate language, suspects or accused persons shall be informed of their rights orally in a language that they understand. A Letter of Rights in a language that they understand shall then be given to them without undue delay.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Any person detained or imprisoned shall be informed in writing, in a simple and accessible language, in a language that s/he understands and immediately, of the facts attributed to him/her and the reasons for his/her deprivation of liberty, as well as his/her rights and specially the following: (...)

When the bill of rights is not available in a language that the detainee understands, s/he will be informed of his/her rights through an interpreter as soon as possible. In this case, the written declaration of rights in a language that s/he understands must be delivered to him/her later and without undue delay.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Letter of Rights in European Arrest Warrant proceedings

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that persons who are arrested for the purpose of the execution of a European Arrest Warrant are provided promptly with an appropriate Letter of Rights containing information on their rights according to the law implementing Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA in the executing Member State.

nationalActs.title: Ley 23/2014, de 20 de noviembre, de reconocimiento mutuo de resoluciones penales en la Unión Europea
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union

provisions.textEn: The detention of a person affected by a European Arrest Warrant shall be carried out in the manner and with the requirements and guarantees provided for in the Criminal Procedural Act.

Once the detained person is brought to justice, s/he will be informed of the existence of the European Arrest Warran, of its contents, of his/her right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing State whose function will be to assist the lawyer in Spain providing him/her with information and advice, of the possibility of consenting irrevocably his/her surrender to the issuing State in the hearing before the judge, as well as of the rest of his/her rights.

items.text: 2. The Letter of Rights shall be drafted in simple and accessible language. An indicative model Letter of Rights is set out in Annex II.

nationalActs.title: Ley 23/2014, de 20 de noviembre, de reconocimiento mutuo de resoluciones penales en la Unión Europea
nationalActs.titleEn: Law on mutual recognition of criminal decisions in the European Union

provisions.comment: The information provided in writing seems limited to the possibility of waiving the lawyer of the issuing State. However, taken into consideration that the guarantees provided for in the Criminal Procedural Law apply to any detained person, also to the person arrested under an European Arrest Warrant, this provision would be fully implemented.
provisions.textEn: The detained person shall be informed in writing in a clear and sufficient manner, and in a simple and understandable language, of his/her right to waive the lawyer in the issuing State, about the content of this right and its consequences, as well as the possibility of its subsequent revocation

items.heading: Article 6
items.subHeading: Right to information about the accusation

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons are provided with information about the criminal act they are suspected or accused of having committed. That information shall be provided promptly and in such detail as is necessary to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings and the effective exercise of the rights of the defence.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
Any person who is charged with a criminal offence may exercise the rights of defence by taking part in the proceedings, as soon as he or she is informed of the procedure, is arrested or is subject to any other precautionary measure or is formally prosecuted, for which purpose he or she shall be informed, without undue delay, of the following rights:

a) Right to be informed of the facts attributed to him/her, as well as of any relevant changes in the object of the investigation and of the alleged facts. This information will be provided with sufficient detail to allow the effective exercise of the right of defence.
In the first Court appearance, the judge will inform the defendant, in the most understandable way, of the facts with which s/he is charged.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons who are arrested or detained are informed of the reasons for their arrest or detention, including the criminal act they are suspected or accused of having committed.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Any person detained or imprisoned shall be informed in writing, in a simple and accessible language, in a language that s/he understands and immediately, of the facts attributed to him/her and the reasons for his/her deprivation of liberty (...)

items.text: 3. Member States shall ensure that, at the latest on submission of the merits of the accusation to a court, detailed information is provided on the accusation, including the nature and legal classification of the criminal offence, as well as the nature of participation by the accused person.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: No express reference is made to information about the nature and legal classification of the criminal offence, as well as the nature of participation by the accused person.
provisions.textEn: In the first court appearance the judge will inform the person under investigation, in the most understandable form, of the facts attributed to him. The Registrar shall inform him beforehand of his rights, in particular those listed in Article 118(1), and shall request him to designate an address in Spain to be summoned, or a person to receive summons on his behalf, with a warning that the summons made to that address or to the person designated shall allow the trial to take place in his absence in the cases provided for in Article 786.

provisions.comment: According to the Criminal Procedural Law, at this time the aforementioned judicial decision is forwarded only to the accusations. However, at a later stage, before the trial takes place, the defendant will be notified, so that s/he can present his/her defense brief.
provisions.textEn: If the Investigating Judge decides that the procedure established in this chapter must be followed, in the same order (according to Article 779.1 4º this order shall contain the determination of the offense and shall identify the person who is accused) will order that the previous proceedings, original or by photocopy, be forwarded to the Prosecutor's Office and to the private accusations, so that, within the common term of ten days, request to proceed to trial by formulating the indictment or to dismiss the case or, exceptionally, to conduct complementary investigative actions.

items.text: 4. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons are informed promptly of any changes in the information given in accordance with this Article where this is necessary to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Any person charged with a punishable act may exercise the right of defence, intervening in the proceedings, since its existence is notified, has been subject to detention or any other precautionary measure or has been indicted. To this end, s/he must be informed, without undue delay, of the following rights: a) Right to be informed of the facts attributed to him/her, as well as of any relevant changes in the object of the investigation and of the alleged facts. This information will be provided with sufficient detail to allow the effective exercise of the right of defence.

When the result of the proceedings produces any relevant change in the object of the investigation and the facts charged, the Judge shall promptly inform the person under investigation.

This information may be provided in the form of a brief statement sufficient to enable the exercise of the rights of defence, communicated in writing to the defence counsel of the person under investigation.

items.heading: Article 7
items.subHeading: Right of access to the materials of the case

items.text: 1. Where a person is arrested and detained at any stage of the criminal proceedings, Member States shall ensure that documents related to the specific case in the possession of the competent authorities which are essential to challenging effectively, in accordance with national law, the lawfulness of the arrest or detention, are made available to arrested persons or to their lawyers.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: Any person detained or imprisoned shall be informed in writing, in a simple and accessible language, in a language that s/he understands and immediately, of the facts attributed to him/her and of the reasons for his/her deprivation of liberty, as well as his/her rights and specially the following: (...) d) Right of access to the elements that are essential to challenge the lawfullness of detention or deprivation of liberty.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that access is granted at least to all material evidence in the possession of the competent authorities, whether for or against suspects or accused persons, to those persons or their lawyers in order to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings and to prepare the defence.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: There is no express reference to the right to access material evidence in the Criminal Procedural Act. The aforementioned article refers to the right to examine proceedings in order to ensure the right of defence. However, the case law interprets such right in connection with the article 24 of the Spanish Constitution, which prohibits the defenselessness of the accused and recognizes the right to use the relevant evidence for his/her defense (e.g. Constitutional Tribunal judgment number 795/2014: According to the jurisprudence, the right of access excludes the pre-investigation phase that is not poured into the process and therefore, lacks virtuality as a source of evidence)
provisions.textEn: Any person charged with a punishable act may exercise the right of defence, intervening in the proceedings, since its existence is notified, has been subject to detention or any other precautionary measure or has been indicted. To this end, s/he must be informed, without undue delay, of the following rights: (...) b) Right to examine the proceedings in due time to safeguard the right of defense and in any case, before a declaration is made.

items.text: 3. Without prejudice to paragraph 1, access to the materials referred to in paragraph 2 shall be granted in due time to allow the effective exercise of the rights of the defence and at the latest upon submission of the merits of the accusation to the judgment of a court. Where further material evidence comes into the possession of the competent authorities, access shall be granted to it in due time to allow for it to be considered.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: There is no express reference to the final part of this Directive provision, according to which "Where further material evidence comes into the possession of the competent authorities, access shall be granted to it in due time to allow for it to be considered".
provisions.textEn: Any person charged with a punishable act may exercise the right of defence, intervening in the proceedings, since its existence is notified, has been subject to detention or any other precautionary measure or has been indicted. To this end, s/he must be informed, without undue delay, of the following rights: (...) b) Right to examine the proceedings in due time to safeguard the right of defense and in any case, before a declaration is made.

items.text: 4. By way of derogation from paragraphs 2 and 3, provided that this does not prejudice the right to a fair trial, access to certain materials may be refused if such access may lead to a serious threat to the life or the fundamental rights of another person or if such refusal is strictly necessary to safeguard an important public interest, such as in cases where access could prejudice an ongoing investigation or seriously harm the national security of the Member State in which the criminal proceedings are instituted. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, a decision to refuse access to certain materials in accordance with this paragraph is taken by a judicial authority or is at least subject to judicial review.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn:
The investigating judge excepcianally may give a reasoned decision on incommunicado detention or imprisonment when any of the following circumstances concur:

a) urgent need to avoid serious consequences that could endanger the life, freedom or physical integrity of a person, or

b) urgent need for immediate action by the investigating judges to avoid seriously compromising the criminal procedure.

In the cases of article 509 (incomunicado detention), the detainee or prisoner may be deprived of the following rights if the circumstances of the case justify it: a) Freely appoint a trusted lawyer. b) Communicate with all or any of the persons with whom s/he has the right to do so, except with the judicial authority, the Prosecutor's Office and the Forensic Physician. c) Interview privately with his/her lawyer. d) Access him/herself or through his/her lawyer to the materials of the case, except the essential elements to be able to challenge the legality of the detention.

The lack of communication or restriction of another right of the previous section will be adopted by judicial order. When the restriction of rights is requested by the Judicial Police or by the Prosecutor's Office, the measures provided for in paragraph 1 shall be adopted for a maximum period of twenty-four hours, within which the judge shall decide on the request, as well as on the need to declare the secret of the investigation procedure. The lack of communication and the application to the detainee or prisoner of any of the exceptions referred to in the previous section will be adopted by court order, and the reasons that justify the adoption of each of the exceptions to the general regime must be motivated in accordance with the provisions of the article 509.

items.text: 5. Access, as referred to in this Article, shall be provided free of charge.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: There is no express reference in the law to gratuity. However, the Order 3/2018, of June 1, on the right of information of those investigated in criminal proceedings, of the State Attorney General's Office, does refer to the access free of charge, although it refers to the possibility that the defendant must bear the expenses only when requesting the material delivery of copies.

items.heading: Article 8

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that when information is provided to suspects or accused persons in accordance with Articles 3 to 6 this is noted using the recording procedure specified in the law of the Member State concerned.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Although there is no express legal provision, when the Police gives the precedent information to the detainee, it will be recorded in the police statement, while when the information is given by the judge,it will be recorded in the minutes drawn up by the Court clerk (Lawyer of the Administration of Justice, formerly called judicial secretary) who is in charge of giving public faith within the Court.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons or their lawyers have the right to challenge, in accordance with procedures in national law, the possible failure or refusal of the competent authorities to provide information in accordance with this Directive.

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.textEn: It is possible to lodge an appeal when the procedure or the judgment has incurred in breach of the rules and procedural guarantees, which will cause defenselessness, if the timely claim for rectification has been made. This claim will not be necessary if the alleged violation involves the violation of a constitutionally guaranteed fundamental right

items.text: Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Union, Member States shall request those responsible for the training of judges, prosecutors, police and judicial staff involved in criminal proceedings to provide appropriate training with respect to the objectives of this Directive.
items.heading: Article 9

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.text:
The sole purpose of this model is to assist national authorities in drawing up their Letter of Rights at national level. Member States are not bound to use this model. When preparing their Letter of Rights, Member States may amend this model in order to align it with their national rules and add further useful information. The Member State’s Letter of Rights must be given upon arrest or detention. This however does not prevent Member States from providing suspects or accused persons with written information in other situations during criminal proceedings.


A. ASSISTANCE OF A LAWYER/ENTITLEMENT TO LEGAL AID


You have the right to speak confidentially to a lawyer. A lawyer is independent from the police. Ask the police if you need help to get in contact with a lawyer, the police shall help you. In certain cases the assistance may be free of charge. Ask the police for more information.


B. INFORMATION ABOUT THE ACCUSATION


You have the right to know why you have been arrested or detained and what you are suspected or accused of having done.


C. INTERPRETATION AND TRANSLATION


If you do not speak or understand the language spoken by the police or other competent authorities, you have the right to be assisted by an interpreter, free of charge. The interpreter may help you to talk to your lawyer and must keep the content of that communication confidential. You have the right to translation of at least the relevant passages of essential documents, including any order by a judge allowing your arrest or keeping you in custody, any charge or indictment and any judgment. You may in some circumstances be provided with an oral translation or summary.


D. RIGHT TO REMAIN SILENT


While questioned by the police or other competent authorities, you do not have to answer questions about the alleged offence. Your lawyer can help you to decide on that.


E. ACCESS TO DOCUMENTS


When you are arrested and detained, you (or your lawyer) have the right to access essential documents you need to challenge the arrest or detention. If your case goes to court, you (or your lawyer) have the right to access the material evidence for or against you.


F. INFORMING SOMEONE ELSE ABOUT YOUR ARREST OR DETENTION/INFORMING YOUR CONSULATE OR EMBASSY


When you are arrested or detained, you should tell the police if you want someone to be informed of your detention, for example a family member or your employer. In certain cases the right to inform another person of your detention may be temporarily restricted. In such cases the police will inform you of this.


If you are a foreigner, tell the police if you want your consular authority or embassy to be informed of your detention. Please also tell the police if you want to contact an official of your consular authority or embassy.


G. URGENT MEDICAL ASSISTANCE


When you are arrested or detained, you have the right to urgent medical assistance. Please let the police know if you are in need of such assistance.


H. PERIOD OF DEPRIVATION OF LIBERTY


After your arrest you may be deprived of liberty or detained for a maximum period of … [fill in applicable number of hours/days]. At the end of that period you must either be released or be heard by a judge who will decide on your further detention. Ask your lawyer or the judge for information about the possibility to challenge your arrest, to review the detention or to ask for provisional release.
items.heading: ANNEX I

nationalActs.title: Real Decreto de 14 de septiembre de 1882 por el que se aprueba la Ley de Enjuiciamiento Criminal

provisions.comment: No reference is made to the right to access the material evidence for or against the defendant. Moreover, although Spanish law requires the detainee to be informed of almost all of the rights that correspond to him/her in writing, the legislation does not contain an annex with an indicative model Letter of Rights and does not use the term "Letter of Rights"
provisions.textEn:
Any person detained or imprisoned will be informed in writing, in a simple and accessible language, in a language that s/he understands and immediately, of the facts attributed to him/her and the reasons for his/her deprivation of liberty, as well as of his/her rights and especially the followings:

a) The right to remain silent by not declaring if s/he does not want to, not to answer any or some of the questions asked, or to state that s/he will only testify before the judge and not before the Police.

b) Right not to testify against oneself and not to confess guilt.

c) The right to appoint a lawyer (...) and to be assisted by him without undue delay. In the event that, due to geographical distance, legal assistance is not immediately possible, telephone or videoconference communication with his/her lawyer will be provided to the detainee, unless such communication is impossible.

d) Right to access the essential elements to challenge the legality of detention or deprivation of liberty.

e) The right to inform the family member or person who wishes, without undue delay, his/her deprivation of liberty and the place of custody in which s/he stays. Foreigners will have the right to have the above circumstances communicated to the consular office of their country.

f) Right to communicate by telephone, without undue delay, with a third party of his/her choice. This communication shall be held in the presence of a police officer or, where appropriate, of the official designated by the judge or prosecutor, without prejudice to Article 527.

g) Right to be visited by the consular authorities of his/her country, to communicate and to mail with them.

h) Right to be assisted free of charge by an interpreter, in the case of a foreigner who does not understand or does not speak Spanish or the official language of the procedure, or in the case of deaf or hearing impaired persons, as well as other persons with language difficulties

i) Right to be recognized by the forensic doctor or his/her legal substitute and, failing that possibility, by the doctor of the institution in which the detainee is located, or by any other doctor dependent of the State or other Public Administrations.

j) Right to request free legal assistance, procedure to do so and conditions to obtain it.

S/he will also be informed of the maximum legal term of detention until being brougt before the judicial authority and the procedure by which s/he may challenge the lawfulness of his/her detention.

When a declaration of rights is not available in a language that the detainee understands, s/he will be informed of his/her rights through an interpreter as soon as it becomes possible. In this case, the written declaration of rights in a language that s/he understand must be submitted to him/her later and without undue delay.

In all cases, the detainee will be allowed to keep in his possession the written declaration of rights during the entire time of the detention.

items.text:
The sole purpose of this model is to assist national authorities in drawing up their Letter of Rights at national level. Member States are not bound to use this model. When preparing their Letter of Rights, Member States may amend this model in order to align it with their national rules and add further useful information.


A. INFORMATION ABOUT THE EUROPEAN ARREST WARRANT


You have the right to be informed about the content of the European Arrest Warrant on the basis of which you have been arrested.


B. ASSISTANCE OF A LAWYER


You have the right to speak confidentially to a lawyer. A lawyer is independent from the police. Ask the police if you need help to get in contact with a lawyer, the police shall help you. In certain cases the assistance may be free of charge. Ask the police for more information.


C. INTERPRETATION AND TRANSLATION


If you do not speak or understand the language spoken by the police or other competent authorities, you have the right to be assisted by an interpreter, free of charge. The interpreter may help you to talk to your lawyer and must keep the content of that communication confidential. You have the right to a translation of the European Arrest Warrant in a language you understand. You may in some circumstances be provided with an oral translation or summary.


D. POSSIBILITY TO CONSENT


You may consent or not consent to being surrendered to the State seeking you. Your consent would speed up the proceedings. [Possible addition of certain Member States: It may be difficult or even impossible to change this decision at a later stage.] Ask the authorities or your lawyer for more information.


E. HEARING


If you do not consent to your surrender, you have the right to be heard by a judicial authority.

provisions.textEn: Once the detained person is brought before the judge, s/he will be informed of the existence of the European arrest warrant, of its contents, of his/her right to appoint a lawyer in the issuing State whose function will consist in providing assistance to the lawyer in Spain by providing information and advice, of the possibility of consenting irrevocably his/her surrender before the judge, as well as of the rest of t his/her rights.

provisions.comment:
These provisions must be completed with the guarantees provided for any detainee in art. 520 of the Criminal Procedure Law.


Although Spanish law requires the arrested person by virtue of an European Arrest Warrant to be informed of almost all of the rights that correspond to him/her in writing, the legislation does not contain an annex with an indicative model Letter of Rights and does not use the term "Letter of Rights".
provisions.textEn: The detained person shall be informed in writing in a clear and sufficient manner, and in a simple and understandable language, of his/her right to resign from the lawyer in the issuing State, about the content of such right and its consequences, as well as of the possibility of revocation.
